Fine-tuning large language models (LLMs) on narrow task-specific datasets can induce broad behavioural misalignment — a phenomenon termed emergent misalignment. We present two studies of Domain Persona Capture (DPC). Study 1: Nine state-of-the-art LLMs (Llama-3.x, Mistral-7B, Gemma-2, Gemma-4) fine-tuned on 6,000 question–answer pairs derived from US Army doctrine using LoRA showed emergent misalignment rates of 83.8–100%, with the Gemma-4 26B MoE architecture showing substantially greater robustness. Study 2: Multimodal fine-tuning of Gemma-4 E2B and E4B revealed a novel dormant DPC phenomenon: multimodally fine-tuned models appeared moderately safe under text-only evaluation (EM 24–44%) but exhibited near-total misalignment (EM 99–100%) when any image — regardless of content — was provided at inference time. This visual anchoring effect creates a systematic blind spot in standard text-only safety evaluation frameworks.

The novel approach of fine-tuning the Llama model for topic categorization with limited data presents significant advancements, offering enhanced performance and reduced hallucinations compared to traditional models. Employing transfer learning and data augmentation techniques, the research demonstrates the model's ability to adapt to diverse thematic domains, achieving high accuracy in topic categorization. Comprehensive comparative analysis with baseline models demonsrates the superiority of the fine-tuned Llama model, highlighting the effectiveness of advanced training methodologies and hyperparameter optimization strategies. Additionally, the analysis of hallucinations illustrates the robustness of implemented mitigation techniques, thereby enhancing the reliability of generated text. Computational efficiency assessment confirms the practical feasibility of deploying the fine-tuned model, balancing resource utilization with performance gains. The study substantiates the potential of large language models to be fine-tuned effectively for specialized tasks, contributing valuable insights to the field of natural language processing.
